title: She was thrown away… after she was used.
paragraphs: She was thrown away… after she was used.

No goodbye.
No protection.
Just a desert… and a dying child.
But here’s the question that should shake you:
What if the place you thought was your ending… is where God finally reveals Himself?
Hagar didn’t plan this life.

She didn’t choose the scandal.
She didn’t choose the pain.
She didn’t choose to be used by people with power and then discarded when it became inconvenient.
She was a servant… caught in someone else’s broken story.

And suddenly—
she’s pregnant, hated, mistreated, and running for her life into the wilderness.
Pause.
Because this is not just ancient history.
This is you.

The moment you gave your heart to something that didn’t honor God.
The moment you became “useful” to people… but never truly loved.
The moment you realized—too late—that you were part of something messy, sinful, and out of control.
Now you’re left carrying the consequences.
Alone.
Ashamed.
Confused.
Shame is loud in the desert.
It whispers:

“You should’ve known better.”
“You are the problem.”
“You are forgotten.”

And if you listen long enough…
you start to believe that God has moved on without you.
That your story is now defined by your worst moment.
That you are no longer worth redeeming.
But then something happens in Genesis 16 that breaks every lie.
“The angel of the Lord found her by a spring of water in the wilderness…” (Genesis 16:7)
Found her.

Not ignored.
Not avoided.
Not rejected.
Found.
Let that hit you.

God did not wait for Hagar to fix herself.
He did not say, “Come back when you’re clean.”
He went into the wilderness… and met her there.
And then He asked:
“Hagar… where have you come from and where are you going?” (Genesis 16:8)
God already knew the answer.
But He wanted her heart.
Because healing begins when honesty is spoken in the presence of God.
And Hagar does something radical.
She gives God a name.
“You are a God of seeing… Truly here I have seen Him who looks after me.” (Genesis 16:13)
El Roi.
The God who sees me.

Not the version I pretend to be.
Not the filtered version for people.
The real me.

Broken.
Messy.
Regretful.
Seen.
But the story doesn’t end there.
Because shame has a way of circling back.
Genesis 21.
She’s cast out again.

No shelter.
No security.
Just a bottle of water… and a child slowly dying under the desert sun.
“She sat down opposite him… for she said, ‘Let me not look on the death of the child.’ And as she sat opposite him, she lifted up her voice and wept.” (Genesis 21:16)
This is not polished faith.
This is raw despair.

This is the moment where your prayers don’t sound holy…
they sound like breaking.
And here’s the turning point.
“And God heard the voice of the boy… Fear not, for God has heard…” (Genesis 21:17)
Then this:
“Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water…” (Genesis 21:19)
Don’t miss this.
The well was already there.
She just couldn’t see it.
Some scholars interpret this as a supernatural provision appearing in that moment. Others see it as God revealing what was already present but hidden by despair.
Either way—the message is the same:
God provides… even when you feel abandoned.
And sometimes your biggest problem isn’t that God is absent.
It’s that pain has blinded you to His provision.
Let’s go deeper.
Hagar’s story is not just about survival.
It’s about the human condition.
Because every one of us has stepped into a story marked by sin.

Maybe not Hagar’s exact situation—
but the same root:

Disobedience.
Broken desires.
Self-reliance.
Compromise.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)
And sin always leads somewhere.

A desert.
A drought.
A distance from God.
But here is where everything shifts.

Because the God who saw Hagar…
is the same God who sent Jesus.
And Jesus didn’t just walk into a desert.
He walked into our sin.
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
Catch that.

Not when you cleaned yourself up.
Not when you fixed your reputation.
While you were still in it.

Jesus took the shame.
The rejection.
The consequence of sin.

On the cross, He was treated like the outcast…
so you could be brought in.
Hagar found a well.
But Jesus said something greater:
“Whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never be thirsty again.” (John 4:14)
This is not temporary relief.
This is eternal restoration.
Not just surviving your mistakes—
being redeemed from them.
So let me ask you, heart to heart:
Where are you right now?

Still running?
Still hiding?
Still carrying shame that Jesus already paid for?
You don’t have to stay in the desert.
But you do have to respond.

Repent—not just feeling bad, but turning back to God.
Release the pride that says you can fix yourself.
Receive the grace that was bought by Christ alone.
God sees you.
Not to condemn you—
but to call you back.
Not to expose you—
but to restore you.
This is your interruption.
This is your invitation.
Come back to Jesus.
Let Him open your eyes again.
Let Him show you the well you thought didn’t exist.
If this pierced your heart, don’t ignore it.
